description: Interactive MCQ review quiz for Grade 7 Mathematics — Chapter 5 'Connecting the Dots' (Statistics). Card-based quiz layout with progress indicator, immediate feedback with explanations, and results dashboard with circular progress ring. Covers arithmetic mean, median, outliers, bar graphs, statistical questions, zero vs no value, and choosing the right measure. Redesigned per Singularity Design System — Poppins font, #4A4DC9 primary, #FF7212 accent, purple-to-orange gradient buttons, pill shapes, floating geometric decorations. Indian school context.
subject: Mathematics

instructionsForStudent.default: Answer all 8 questions covering mean, median, outliers, bar graphs, and statistical questions. Take your time — read each question and all options carefully before selecting your answer. After each question, read the explanation to reinforce your understanding.

teachingNotes.default: This is a summative review quiz. Let the student attempt all questions independently first. After each answer, the tool provides immediate feedback. At the end, review any incorrect answers. Q4 (outlier direction) and Q6 (zero vs no value) are the most commonly missed — spend extra time on these if the student gets them wrong. Q7 (door height = maximum, not mean) connects to the 'A Mean Decision!' lesson from the chapter. After the quiz, ask: 'Which concept from this chapter surprised you the most?'

defaultQuestions.question: Virat scored 45, 32, 67, 12, and 94 runs in five innings. What is his arithmetic mean (average) score?
The daily prices (₹/kg) of tomatoes at a sabzi mandi over a week are: 18, 22, 25, 28, 30, 35, 40. What is the median price?
defaultQuestions.explanation: Sorted data has 7 values (odd). Median = 4th value = ₹28.

defaultQuestions.question: Six students scored 12, 15, 18, 22, 25, 30 in a quiz. What is the median score?
Heights of a family: 170, 168, 172, 165, 95 cm (a toddler). The outlier 95 cm pulls the mean ______ the median.
defaultQuestions.explanation: A low outlier drags the mean downward, so mean < median.

defaultQuestions.question: Which of these is a statistical question?
options: How many runs did India score today?
How tall are Grade 7 students in our school?
defaultQuestions.explanation: A statistical question expects variability and requires data collection.

defaultQuestions.question: A cricketer's scores: 57, 13, 0, 84, —, 51. The '—' means did not play. To find the mean, divide total by:
defaultQuestions.explanation: Zero is a valid score; '—' is no participation. Divide by 5 matches played.

defaultQuestions.question: A family wants to build a door. Heights: 160, 155, 170, 175, 168 cm. Which measure for door height?
defaultQuestions.explanation: A door must be tall enough for the tallest person — use maximum, not mean!

defaultQuestions.question: In a clustered bar graph comparing onion prices in two towns, placing bars side-by-side helps us:
options: Compare month-wise prices at a glance
defaultQuestions.explanation: Clustered bar graphs make visual comparison of categories easy by placing bars side by side.
